en: The Hymn to Śiva Composed by Upamanyu
Victory to you, O Śaṅkara, Lord of Pārvatī, Mṛḍa, Śambhu, adorned with the crescent moon! O Destroyer of Madana, lover of your devotees, beloved of Kailāsa, ocean of the nectar of compassion!
[I am] unskilled in discourses on the true means, my heart shattered by the arrow of sorrow.
I go for refuge to the Lord, the worthy protector, who is adorned with the crescent moon as his crest-ornament. O Lord,
like the Sun, the master of the day, arise even slightly within the sky of our hearts with Your own splendor, to dispel the great, spreading darkness that obstructs vision.
We are not capable of even perceiving your path with our physical eyes;
O Lord, look upon us quickly with your all-encompassing eye that grants fearlessness out of compassion.
O Lord, the mere remembrance of you is purifying; it is not possible to adequately describe you through words joined with praise.
For milk is indeed sweet by its very nature; how much more so when mixed with white sugar?
(5) Even though you bear the skull of Śava as an ornament, you act as nectar; even though you possess three eyes, you are the purifier.
Though you have uneven eyes, you are Bhava himself, the ender of worldly existence, for those who possess equal vision. (6)
Though bearing the trident, you are free from ailment; though devoted to firm dispassion, you possess passion;
though moving about as a beggar, you are the Great Lord—O Lord, this conduct of yours is indeed wondrous! For the wish-fulfilling tree, when merely beheld, bestows whatever is desired.

O Wise One, as soon as you are remembered in the heart, you become the bestower of desired fruits to those who bow before you. (8) Before Death suddenly seizes me with his serpent-noose, grant me quickly freedom from fear; for once my life has departed, what is the use of medicines? (9)
Enough with these sense-objects, which wound me like fearsome venomous serpents;
quickly drench me with your compassionate glances, as if with nectars, in my state of agitation.
Many sages have today been led to blessedness, having beheld the object of their own desire.
O Source of Compassion, surely look with Your eye upon me who am thus despondent.
I bow down; yet to whom else shall I go for refuge, other than You who grant fearlessness to the wretched?
O Lord, like one separated from his beloved, I perceive this entire world as consisting of You.
O Lord, you have shown compassion to many; why then do you not show compassion to me?
Is an atom difficult for the Tortoise to bear when he is supporting Mount Mandara?
(13) If you consider me impure, why is this skull held as an ornament upon your head?
Moreover, are you not a double-tongued serpent bearing the poison-mark of association with the wicked?
(14) Where shall I cast my gaze? What shall I do? How shall I conduct myself, overwhelmed as I am by fear?
Where indeed do you dwell? Protect me! Protect me! O Śambhu, I have come to you for refuge. (15)
Why do I roll upon the ground in agitation? Why do I beat my chest or cut off my head?
Why do I weep or cry out so piteously, O Lord, if You do not look upon me?
O Śiva, omnipresent Śarva, giver of bliss, I bow to You; O God, have mercy on me!
Obeisance to the Lord, the Master, the Lord of the Quarters; O Sovereign, obeisance, obeisance be unto you!
(14) The one who has the young moon as his crest-jewel is my refuge; the Daughter of the Mountain King is my refuge.
Furthermore, both of them are my refuge; I seek no other deity for refuge. (15)
To one who recites this supreme hymn composed by Upamanyu while remaining in the presence of Śambhu,
Śaṅkara bestows the wealth of desired fortune and the highest lifespan.
(16) Whoever should recite this supreme hymn composed by Upamanyu in the vicinity of Śiva...
Having attained the world of Śiva, he rejoices with that very Śiva before long.
Thus ends the hymn to Śiva composed by Upamanyu.
